fullPassage:
After twenty years of filmmaking, I returned to the sea near the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa. Diving in the cold sea, I encountered an extraordinary creature in the dense seaweed forests. It was an octopus. From a heap of shells, the octopus grabbed a fish and ate it. Her cleverness amazed me. When she sensed danger, she hid by wrapping seaweed around herself. I placed my camera near her den and visited regularly, mapping the environment around me.

After about a month, the octopus came near me. She reached out and waved like a human friend. Then she covered my hand and rode to the surface on my hand. This sparked my curiosity, and I was filled with amazement. I learned that "it" was actually "she." Her marvelous behavior changed my perspective completely.

One day, a pyjama shark attacked her and took a bite of one of her arms. She escaped into a crack in the rocks, bleeding. I was relieved when the shark lost interest and swam away. She returned to her den without one arm. I learned that an octopus’s arms function like hands, legs, a nose, and eyes all at once. Losing one was a serious blow, but she survived.

Over the following weeks, the wound healed and her arm grew back. She became active again, hunting and exploring as before. Witnessing her recovery, I compared my own life. I started spending more time with my family and began diving with my son, sharing this unforgiving but beautiful underwater world.

An octopus lives on average about one year, and its life ends after reproducing. At about eight months, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet. After mating, she stayed in her den without feeding or hunting. She had timed her death for the hatching of her eggs. When the eggs hatched, she died. It was a noble sacrifice. Months later, my son found a little octopus near the same den.

She was smart, sensitive, and strong. She was committed to protecting the birth of her young. Her sacrifice was not that of simply an octopus, but of a creature deeply connected to this world. She taught me that we are all part of this extraordinary planet.

Seaweed can be used as an alternative to plastic coating for hamburger packages. Eco-friendly leather made from pineapple leaves, grape waste, and mushroom is gaining popularity. The market for eco-friendly leather was valued at $725 million in 2022 and is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030.

questions.passage: After twenty years of filmmaking, I returned to the sea near the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa. __________ in the cold sea, I encountered an extraordinary creature in the dense seaweed forests.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주절(I encountered)과 동시에 일어나는 동작을 나타내는 분사구문 Diving이 적절하다. "차가운 바다에서 다이빙하면서"
det.analysis:
✅ ③ Diving: 동시동작 분사구문(현재분사)
❌ ① Dive: 동사원형 단독 사용 불가
❌ ② Dived: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ④ To dive: to부정사 → 동시동작 표현에 부적절
det.tip: 분사구문 (동시동작): ~ing ..., 주절 → 주절과 동시에 일어나는 동작

questions.passage: Her cleverness amazed me. When she sensed danger, she hid by __________ seaweed around herself. I placed my camera near her den and visited regularly.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(~ing)가 와야 한다. wrapping(감싸면서)이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② wrapping: 전치사 by + 동명사 → 수단/방법
❌ ① wrap: 원형 → 전치사 뒤 불가
❌ ③ wrapped: 과거형 → 전치사 뒤 불가
❌ ④ to wrap: to부정사 → by 뒤에 부적절
det.tip: by + ~ing: ~함으로써 (수단/방법을 나타내는 전치사 + 동명사)

questions.passage: I learned that an octopus’s arms function like hands, legs, a nose, and eyes all at once. Losing one was a serious blow __________ threatened her survival, but she survived.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 선행사 a serious blow(사물)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ that: 사물 선행사(a serious blow) + 주격 관계대명사
❌ ① what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 → 앞에 선행사가 있으므로 불가
❌ ② who: 사람 선행사용 → blow는 사물
❌ ④ where: 관계부사 → 뒤에 완전한 절이 와야 하나 threatened의 주어 필요
det.tip: 선행사(사물) + that/which + 동사: 사물을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사

questions.passage: Witnessing her recovery, I compared my own life. I started spending more time with my family and began diving with my son, __________ this unforgiving but beautiful underwater world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 앞 절의 부대상황/결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로 현재분사 sharing이 적절하다. "아들과 다이빙하면서, 이 세계를 공유하며"
det.analysis:
✅ ② sharing: 동시동작/부대상황 분사구문 (현재분사)
❌ ① shared: 과거형 → 접속사 없이 두 절 연결 불가
❌ ③ to share: to부정사 → 동시동작 표현에 부적절
❌ ④ having shared: 완료 분사구문 → 주절보다 앞선 동작이 아님
❌ ⑤ share: 원형 → 문법적으로 불가
det.tip: 부대상황 분사구문: 주절, ~ing ... → 주절과 동시에 진행되는 동작

questions.passage: After about a month, the octopus ①<u>came</u> near me. She reached out and ②<u>waved</u> like a human friend. Then she covered my hand and ③<u>was ridden</u> to the surface on my hand. This ④<u>sparked</u> my curiosity, and I was ⑤<u>filled</u> with amazement.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ was ridden → rode: 문어가 내 손 위에 올라타서 수면까지 갔다(능동). "She rode to the surface on my hand."
det.analysis:
❌ ③ was ridden(수동) → rode(능동): 문어가 스스로 올라탄 것(능동)
✅ ① came: 과거형 동사 → "가까이 왔다" 올바름
✅ ② waved: 과거형 동사 → "손을 흔들었다" 올바름
✅ ④ sparked: 과거형 동사 → "호기심을 자극했다" 올바름
✅ ⑤ filled: 수동 → "경이로움으로 채워졌다" 올바름
det.tip: 능동/수동 구분: 주어가 동작의 주체(능동 rode) vs. 동작을 당하는 쪽(수동 was ridden)

questions.passage: After twenty years of filmmaking, I returned to the sea near the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa. Diving in the cold sea, I encountered an extraordinary creature in the dense seaweed forests. It was an octopus. From a heap of shells, the octopus grabbed a fish and ate it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "From a heap of shells, the octopus grabbed a fish and ate it." → 문어가 조개 무더기에서 물고기를 잡아먹었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 조개 무더기에서 물고기를 잡아먹음: 본문과 일치
❌ ① Cape of Good Hope(희망봉)이지 Cape Town이 아님
❌ ③ "placed my camera near her den" → 굴 안이 아니라 굴 근처
❌ ④ "wrapping seaweed around herself" → 모래가 아니라 해초로 몸을 감쌈
det.tip: 내용 일치: 각 선택지의 핵심 단어를 본문과 정확히 대조

ch: 화자는 처음 만난 날 문어의 굴 안에 카메라를 넣었다.
문어는 위험을 느끼면 모래 속에 숨었다.

questions.passage: One day, a pyjama shark attacked her and took a bite of one of her arms. She escaped into a crack in the rocks, bleeding. I was relieved when the shark lost interest and swam away. She returned to her den without one arm. I learned that an octopus’s arms function like hands, legs, a nose, and eyes all at once. Losing one was a serious blow, but she survived.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "the shark lost interest and swam away" → 상어는 흥미를 잃고 떠났다. 따라서 "끝까지 추적하여 잡았다"는 본문과 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 상어가 끝까지 추적: "lost interest and swam away" → 흥미를 잃고 떠남
✅ ① "took a bite of one of her arms" → 팔 하나를 물음
✅ ② "escaped into a crack" → 바위 틈으로 도망
✅ ④ "returned to her den without one arm" → 팔 하나 없이 돌아옴
det.tip: 불일치 문제: "끝까지 추적" vs. "lost interest(흥미를 잃음)" 핵심 동사 대조

ch: 파자마 상어가 문어의 팔 하나를 물었다.
문어는 팔 하나 없이 굴로 돌아왔다.

questions.passage: She was smart, sensitive, and strong. She was committed to protecting the birth of her young. Her sacrifice was not that of simply an octopus, but of a creature deeply connected to this world. She taught me that we are all part of this extraordinary planet.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "She taught me that we are all part of this extraordinary planet" → 문어와의 교감을 통해 삶의 소중한 깨달음을 얻은 이야기
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 문어와의 교감을 통한 깨달음: 가족과 시간을 보내고 자연과의 연결을 깨달음
❌ ① 생물학적 분류: 본문의 주제 아님
❌ ② 생태계 위기: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 촬영 기법: 본문의 보조 소재일 뿐
❌ ⑤ 번식 생태: 부분적 소재이지 주제 아님
det.tip: 글의 주제: 결론부 "She taught me..."에서 핵심 메시지가 드러남

questions.passage: An octopus lives on average about one year, and its life ends after reproducing. After mating, she stayed in her den without feeding or hunting. She had timed her death for the hatching of her eggs. When the eggs hatched, she died. It was __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새끼의 탄생을 위해 먹이도 먹지 않고 목숨을 바친 것은 고귀한 희생(a noble sacrifice)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② a noble sacrifice: 새끼를 위해 목숨을 바침 = 고귀한 희생
❌ ① a clever trick: 속임수가 아닌 희생
❌ ③ a lucky escape: 탈출이 아님
❌ ④ a natural instinct: 본능이라 할 수도 있으나 본문의 어조상 "noble sacrifice"가 정답
det.tip: "timed her death for the hatching" → 죽음의 시기를 맞춤 = 의도적 희생

questions.passage: She was smart, sensitive, and strong. She was __________ to protecting the birth of her young. Her sacrifice was not that of simply an octopus, but of a creature deeply connected to this world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새끼의 탄생을 보호하는 데 헌신적인(committed)이었다. 먹이도 먹지 않고 알이 부화할 때까지 지켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② committed: "committed to ~ing" = ~에 헌신적인 → 문맥 일치
❌ ① indifferent(무관심한): 헌신의 반대
❌ ③ hostile(적대적인): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ reluctant(꺼리는): 헌신적 행동과 모순
det.tip: be committed to + ~ing: ~에 헌신하다/전념하다

questions.passage: Seaweed can be used as an __________ to plastic coating for hamburger packages. Eco-friendly leather made from pineapple leaves, grape waste, and mushroom is gaining popularity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 해초를 플라스틱 코팅의 대안(alternative)으로 사용할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① alternative(대안): 플라스틱 대신 사용 = 대안
❌ ② addition(추가): 대체가 아닌 추가
❌ ③ obstacle(장애물): 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ threat(위협): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: an alternative to ~: ~에 대한 대안 → 기존 것을 대체하는 새로운 방법

questions.passage: From a heap of shells, the octopus grabbed a fish and ate it. Her cleverness __________ (amaze) me. When she sensed danger, she hid by wrapping seaweed around herself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: amaze(동사) → amazed(과거형): 과거 시제 서술. "그녀의 영리함이 나를 놀라게 했다"
det.analysis:
amaze(동사) → amazed(과거형)
문맥상 과거 시제(returned, encountered와 같은 시제)
Her cleverness amazed me = 그녀의 영리함이 나를 놀라게 했다
det.tip: 과거 서술문에서 동사의 시제를 일치시키기: returned, encountered, amazed

questions.passage: One day, a pyjama shark attacked her and took a bite of one of her arms. She escaped into a crack in the rocks, __________ (bleed).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: bleed(동사) → bleeding(현재분사): 분사구문으로 "피를 흘리면서" 도망쳤다는 동시동작 표현
det.analysis:
bleed(동사) → bleeding(현재분사)
바위 틈으로 도망치는 동작과 동시에 피를 흘림
분사구문: escaped ..., bleeding = 피를 흘리면서 도망쳤다
det.tip: 동시동작 분사구문: 주절, ~ing → "~하면서"

questions.stem: 다음 글에서 문어가 화자의 손을 덮고 수면까지 올라간 행동이 화자에게 불러일으킨 감정을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "This sparked my curiosity" → 호기심 = curiosity
det.analysis:
문어의 행동 → "sparked my curiosity" = 호기심을 자극했다
1단어 답 = curiosity
det.tip: spark one's curiosity = 호기심을 자극하다/불러일으키다

det.korean: "It was a noble sacrifice" → 고귀한 희생 = sacrifice
det.analysis:
먹이도 먹지 않고 알 부화를 위해 죽음 = noble sacrifice
1단어 답 = sacrifice
det.tip: sacrifice = 희생 — 자신의 것을 포기하여 다른 것을 위해 바치는 행위

After mating, she stayed in her den without feeding or hunting. She had timed her death for the hatching of her eggs. When the eggs hatched, she died. It was a noble sacrifice. questions.stem: 다음 글에서 문어가 죽은 뒤 몇 달 후 화자의 아들이 같은 굴 근처에서 발견한 것을 본문에서 3단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "my son found a little octopus near the same den" → 작은 문어 = a little octopus
det.analysis:
아들이 발견한 것 = a little octopus (같은 굴 근처)
3단어 답 = a little octopus
det.tip: "본문에서 찾기" 유형: 핵심 동사(found) 뒤의 목적어를 정확히 찾기

questions.passage: After twenty years of filmmaking, I returned to the sea near the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa. Diving in the cold sea, I encountered an extraordinary creature in the dense seaweed forests. It was an octopus. From a heap of shells, the octopus grabbed a fish and ate it. questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The narrator encountered the octopus in the dense seaweed forests near the Cape of Good Hope."

det.korean: "I encountered an extraordinary creature in the dense seaweed forests" + "near the Cape of Good Hope" → 희망봉 근처 빽빽한 해초 숲에서 문어를 만남. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문의 두 표현을 결합하면 진술과 정확히 일치
det.tip: 두 문장의 정보를 결합하여 진술과 대조

questions.passage: One day, a pyjama shark attacked her and took a bite of one of her arms. She escaped into a crack in the rocks, bleeding. I was relieved when the shark lost interest and swam away. She returned to her den without one arm. I learned that an octopus’s arms function like hands, legs, a nose, and eyes all at once. Losing one was a serious blow, but she survived.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The octopus lost her arm permanently and never recovered."

det.korean: 본문(P4): "the wound healed and her arm grew back" → 상처가 치유되고 팔이 다시 자랐다. "영구적으로 잃었다"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: "her arm grew back" → 팔이 재생됨 ≠ "permanently" + "never recovered"
det.tip: permanently(영구적으로)와 grew back(다시 자랐다)은 모순 → False

"The market for eco-friendly leather is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030."

det.korean: "is expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030" → 본문과 정확히 일치 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 원문 "expected to reach $1.2 billion by 2030"과 진술이 정확히 일치
det.tip: 본문의 수치를 그대로 인용한 진술 → True

Months later, my son found a little octopus near the same den.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The octopus died before her eggs hatched."

det.korean: 본문: "She had timed her death for the hatching of her eggs. When the eggs hatched, she died." → 알이 부화했을 때 죽었다. 알이 부화하기 전에 죽은 것이 아니다. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: "When the eggs hatched, she died" → 부화와 동시에/부화 후 죽음 ≠ "before hatched"
det.tip: 시간 순서: 알 부화 → 죽음 (before가 아닌 when/after)
